newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil plans to take EU chicken, turkey row to WTO. [CORRECTED 13:06 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Brazil plans to take EU chicken, turkey row to WTO. [CORRECTED 13:06 GMT]

text.p: Brazil will seek formal consultations before the World Trade Organization (WTO) over European Union (EU) trade practices, saying its chicken and turkey exports are being discriminated against, (corrects from "it is being hurt by chicken and turkey imports from Europe"), a local newspaper reported.

Gazeta Mercantil said the Brazilian government claims the EU is using subjective criteria to decide what countries may benefit from a zero import tariff on chicken and turkey and, as a result, is buying very little from Brazil.
"We have already dealt with the issue bilaterally in informal discussions," Jose Alfredo Graca Lima, the Brazilian Foreign Ministry's economics department chief, was quoted as saying.
"On those occasions, the European Union demonstrated understanding but did not offer any concrete solution to the problem," he added.

The paper said Brazil decided in July to enter the consultation request against the EU and since then has been preparing the case it will bring before the WTO, which may include a request for arbitration.
The EU established its system of quotas for zero tariffs on chicken and turkey imports in 1992 to compensate countries who felt they were being hurt by its subsidy regime, Gazeta added.
